---
# A page title, not decoration, and it does two jobs.
#
# 1. The metadata surfaces. Quarto composes `<title>`, `og:title` and
#    `twitter:title` from this plus the site title. With `title: ""` the two
#    social surfaces rendered as "– Robbins Analytics" — a dangling separator on
#    every shared card and every scrape of the landing page — while `<title>`
#    fell back to the bare site title. Every other page on the site carries a
#    title and rendered correctly; only the landing page did not.
#
# 2. The hero's own H1. With no title metadata, Quarto promotes the document's
#    first level-1 heading to be the title — so `# Aaron Robbins` was lifted OUT
#    of the hero into the title block above it, and the hero rendered starting
#    at the subtitle with no name in it. Setting a title here leaves the
#    heading where it was written.
#
# `body-classes` is the third piece: with a title set, Quarto renders its own
# title block, which would restate the name twice. felix.scss hides it on
# felix-home (styles.scss did the same on hero-page). `title-block-style: none`
# is NOT the way to do that — it still emits the heading AND emits a second
# <header id="title-block-header">, which is a duplicate id and an axe failure.
title: "Aaron Robbins, AI Analytics Architect"
# The social titles are set explicitly because Quarto otherwise composes
# "<title> – <site title>" with an en dash; the spec (2026-10-14) wants a
# pipe on the cards. The <title> element itself keeps Quarto's composed form
# (`pagetitle:` does not remove the site title; tried 2026-10-14), which is
# what every other page carries. The description is the site-wide one in
# _quarto.yml, restated here so this page never falls back to anything else.
open-graph:
  title: "Aaron Robbins, AI Analytics Architect | Robbins Analytics"
  description: "AI analytics architecture portfolio, Aaron Robbins. Governed analytics, built with AI and proven by tests."
twitter-card:
  title: "Aaron Robbins, AI Analytics Architect | Robbins Analytics"
  description: "AI analytics architecture portfolio, Aaron Robbins. Governed analytics, built with AI and proven by tests."
# felix-home scopes the Felix page styling (paper, Inter, Inter Tight) to this
# page; see felix.scss. hero-page is kept so styles.scss's title-block rule
# still applies if felix.scss is ever removed.
body-classes: hero-page felix-home
image: https://www.robbinsanalytics.com/assets/thumb-portfolio.png
# custom, not full: the Felix sections carry their own 76rem container, and
# Quarto's page grid would add a second set of gutters around it.
page-layout: custom
toc: false
image-alt: "Cascadia module card — title, one-line summary, and the data source."
# Four listings over one inventory, one template. Quarto hands a custom
# template `items`, `template-params` and `utils`, never the listing itself,
# so each names its group here. The template always receives the whole
# inventory sorted by `order`, so a card's number is its position in the
# index whichever page it appears on. See _templates/fx-card.ejs.
listing:
  - id: fx-feature
    contents: data/portfolio.yml
    template: _templates/fx-card.ejs
    sort: "order"
    page-size: 100
    template-params:
      group: feature
      slug: build-by-build
      heading: h3
  - id: fx-leadership
    contents: data/portfolio.yml
    template: _templates/fx-card.ejs
    sort: "order"
    page-size: 100
    template-params:
      group: leadership
      display-order: [validation-playbook, operating-charter]
      slug: build-by-build
      heading: h4
  - id: fx-featured
    contents: data/portfolio.yml
    template: _templates/fx-card.ejs
    sort: "order"
    page-size: 100
    template-params:
      group: featured
      heading: h4
  - id: fx-beyond
    contents: data/portfolio.yml
    template: _templates/fx-card.ejs
    sort: "order"
    page-size: 100
    template-params:
      group: beyond
      heading: h4
---

## Specify, [validate]{.fx-serif}, operate
:::

[Explore the Cascadia operating system <span class="fx-arrow--disc" aria-hidden="true">&#8599;</span>](cascadia/index.html){.fx-disc-link}
:::

```{=html}
<ol class="fx-tiles">
  <li class="fx-tile">
    <div class="fx-tile__top"><p class="fx-tile__num">01<span>Specify</span></p><a class="fx-pill" href="https://www.robbinsanalytics.com/cascadia-validation-playbook/">Validation Playbook</a></div>
    <h3 class="fx-tile__title">Written <span class="fx-tile__muted">spec</span></h3>
    <p class="fx-tile__flow">Specification &#8594; agent build &#8594; review</p>
    <p class="fx-tile__text">I set the architecture, the data model and the measurement definitions as a written specification. AI coding agents build to it. I do not hand-write the Python: I write the spec, review the output and validate it.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="fx-tile">
    <div class="fx-tile__top"><p class="fx-tile__num">02<span>Validate</span></p><a class="fx-pill" href="/projects/cascadia-revenue-assurance.html">Revenue Assurance</a></div>
    <h3 class="fx-tile__title">Independent <span class="fx-tile__muted">check</span></h3>
    <p class="fx-tile__flow">Definition &#8594; independent SQL &#8594; reconcile</p>
    <p class="fx-tile__text">A separately written calculation checks a published figure against its definition. Revenue Assurance derives every published cell twice, by two engines written to be different, and they agree. Claim Integrity also publishes its numerical agreement and the separate limits of its assurance record.</p>
  </li>
  <li class="fx-tile">
    <div class="fx-tile__top"><p class="fx-tile__num">03<span>Operate</span></p><a class="fx-pill" href="/projects/cascadia-matter-ledger.html">Matter Ledger</a></div>
    <h3 class="fx-tile__title">Operated, not <span class="fx-tile__muted">only built</span></h3>
    <p class="fx-tile__flow">Schedule &#8594; re-assert &#8594; publish failures</p>
    <p class="fx-tile__text">A surface that has only ever shown green has demonstrated nothing. Matter Ledger runs on a schedule, re-asserts its own invariants on every run, reconciles a live increment against the frozen baseline, and publishes the result, including when a run fails.</p>
  </li>
</ol>
```
